newsitem.title: USA: U.S. beef exports expected to rise in 1997 - USMEF.
newsitem.headline: U.S. beef exports expected to rise in 1997 - USMEF.

text.p: U.S. exports of beef and beef variety meats could climb above the magical mark of one million tonnes for the first time in 1997, according to the U.S. Meat Export Federation (USMEF).
USMEF has set a 1997 goal of 1.17 million tonnes, up from 982,000 tonnes last year, the federation said in a statement issued at the National Cattlemen's Beef Association annual convention here.

"It won't be easy but we think this is a realistic goal for us to work for. Barring some unforeseen catastrophe we expect U.S. beef sales to increase next year in all major export markets," president and CEO Philip Seng said.
He said MEF had met its export goal in two of the last three years with 1996 the exception. USMEF's goal for 1996 was 1,094,000 tonnes.
"In key markets, like Japan, Korea, Hong Kong and Taiwan, beef consumption dropped significantly with news of BSE in Europe and the E.coli 0157:H7 epidemic in Japan," he said.
Seng said USMEF devoted funds to a food safety campaign in Japan last year and expected the marketing climate to be more conducive to growth in 1997.
